claims.text: The paper formally conjectures that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal. [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document]

groundings.excerpt:
14: For a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian permutation \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), Theorem 5.4 supplies two generating sets for the ideal \(J_v\). The authors conjecture:
15: 
16: > **Conjecture.** The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.

claims.text: Conditional on the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, in the boundary subcase \[ p=q-i=1,\qquad c=r-j\ge2,\qquad \min(i,j)=2, \] the degree-\(\le d+2\) quotient of \(Q=J/A_+J\), \(d=ij\), is \[ Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2} \cong \mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2. \] Moreover \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).
This low-degree certificate alone does not imply \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\): a graded abelian group may agree through degree \(d+2\) and have an additional nonzero summand in degree \(d+3\).
